# Lower shock mount uniball replacement

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Replace the lower shock mount uniball by removing the coilover, pressing out the old ball, and installing a new one. [t858]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Jack up the truck.
2. Support the vehicle with a properly sized jack stand.
3. [Partial] Chock the wheel opposite the lifted side.
4. Remove the tire using an impact gun, ratchet, and 21mm socket.
5. Remove the three nuts holding the top of the coilover in place.
6. Remove the lower bolt securing the assembly.
7. [Partial] Slide the entire coilover out from under the truck.
8. Undo the upper ball joint if necessary to clear the UCA.
9. [Partial] Remove the C-clip holding the uniball inside its housing.
10. [Partial] Take off any misalignment spacers first if they are loose enough to come out easily.
11. Press or hammer the old uniball out of the shock eye opening.
12. [Partial] Clean the area thoroughly with parts cleaner and a wire brush.
13. Lightly coat the inside of the coilover eye with grease.
14. Place the new uniball over the greased opening.
15. Slide a washer onto a 1/2x6 grade 8 bolt, then add a 1 1/4 socket to its end.
16. Insert this assembly through the shock eye and into the center of the new uniball.
17. Place a 25mm socket over the protruding bolt head so it sits on top of the uniball.
18. [Partial] Add multiple 1/2 washers and a nut to secure everything together.
19. Use a ratchet to start threading the assembly down until it is square.
20. Strike the setup with an impact gun to drive the uniball fully in place.
21. [Partial] Reinstall the C-clip into the housing groove.
22. [Partial] Put back any misalignment spacers that were removed earlier.
23. [Partial] Reattach the coilover and tighten the upper ball joint nuts to spec.
24. Mount the wheel back onto the hub.
25. Torque the lug bolts or studs to specification.
26. Take a test drive to verify the noise is gone.

_Procedure reported by [t858]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-replace-lower-uniball-on-nisstec-mk84.8163/>_
